body:
The gap the capabilities book has admitted since the quarantine chapter was written, given its own
shard because the ticket it used to cite (T35) landed a DIFFERENT §24.7 slice -- the sequestered
frame -- and is archived. The admission must cite an open ticket, and this is it.

WHAT EXISTS. render-worker.ts runs a bundle in a worker_threads Worker: a hard wall clock (split
spawn/render since T139), resourceLimits on memory, every failure folded to a clean refusal. Its
own header states the honest scope: a Worker bounds the HANG, the crash and the memory. It is NOT
object-capability isolation -- a worker can still import('node:fs') or open a socket.

WHAT THIS TICKET IS. The deeper half: a quarantined renderer that cannot reach the filesystem or
the network at all. Candidate mechanisms the render-worker header already names: SES-in-worker, or
isolated-vm. Each has a real cost (startup, memory, native dependency) that must be measured
against the per-render spawn budget T139 just fought for -- an isolation layer that costs 500ms of
spawn re-creates the flake the split closed.

RAILS, two-sided like every reach rail: a bundle that imports node:fs or dials out is refused or
finds nothing, AND the ordinary OK bundle still renders inside its budgets on both platforms.

UNTIL IT LANDS the book's admission stays, citing this id: the code is bounded but trusted not to
reach.
title: Confine a quarantined renderer from the filesystem and the network — the ocap half of the sandbox
